concerns.text: T026a implements 'Learned Sparse (RTPurbo) baseline runner' but the spec (FR-008) and plan explicitly mandate evaluating the Learned Sparse baseline over 5 independent random seeds to account for training variance. The task description does not explicitly require running 5 seeds or aggregating them, risking a semantic weakening of FR-008 where a single run might be accepted as the baseline.

T029 implements the statistical test but relies on T019c (Static) and T026b (Learned). T026b is the aggregation of the 5 seeds. If T026a (the runner) does not strictly enforce the 5-seed requirement, T029 will perform a paired t-test on insufficient data, violating FR-006 and SC-004 which require statistical validity against a multi-seed baseline.

T012 mentions 'CPU-only quantization (e.g., low-bit)' as a constraint. The spec (FR-002) and plan require running a 'frozen Llama-3-8B model'. While quantization is a valid optimization, the task must explicitly ensure that the quantization method does not alter the attention map distribution significantly enough to invalidate the 'ground truth' labels. A semantic weakening occurs if the quantization introduces noise that makes the 'RTPurbo-selected tokens' unreliable, violating the ground truth integrity required by US-1.

T033 (Cross-Model Validation) is marked as unchecked (not started). The plan and spec (FR-008, SC-006) explicitly mandate Cross-Model Validation on Gemma-2 to test generalizability. Leaving this task unchecked in the tasks list for a 'tasked' stage implies the deliverable is missing, which is a direct violation of the plan's requirement to validate the hypothesis beyond a single model.

T031 implements the Falsifiability Check against the '<1% threshold'. The Constitution (Principle VI) and Plan (FR-009) mandate this check. However, T031 depends on T027 (Static metrics) and T026a (Learned metrics). If T026a does not strictly enforce the 5-seed aggregation (see T026a concern), the performance drop calculated in T031 will be statistically invalid, weakening the falsifiability constraint.
